messages:
sam: Heads-up — we got a 15m 429 spike in us-west at ~1779001200. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/qo3X/rate-limits (saw multiple orgs, but one API key accounts for ~65% of 429s)
ops-bot: ALERT: High 429 rate detected in cluster us-west (5m avg > 6%). Incident ID: INC-2026-0318-01 :rotating_light:
alisha: Thanks. Is this a quota exhaustion or a burst token refill issue?
mike: Quick look: per-org qps looks fine. Per-key token_bucket.burst used = 1.0 for that key, refill_rate suspiciously low in traces.
eva: I pulled the trace for key=k_9f2a — lots of short-lived concurrent requests (clients retrying). Likely client-side fanout.
alisha: Ok. Two angles: 1) detect per-key burst anomalies and alert earlier, 2) add soft-block and CS playbook to reach out to customer.
sam: Can we add an Alertmanager rule for per-key 429 concentration? e.g. if one key >50% of 429s in 5m and overall 429 > 3% -> page on-call.
mike: Draft rule (Prometheus):
```
- alert: PerKey429Concentration
  expr: (
    sum by (api_key) (increase(api_http_responses_total{code="429"}[5m]))
    / sum(increase(api_http_responses_total[5m]))
  ) > 0.5 and sum(increase(api_http_responses_total[5m])) > 50
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Single API key generating >50% of 429s (5m)"
    description: "Check key label, contact CS, consider short token_bucket reduction for that key."
```
alisha: Nice. Also add a derived metric: per_key_retry_ratio = retries/inbound_requests by key. If >0.2 + 429 concentration -> auto-create CS ticket.
eva: For dashboard: add a panel showing top-10 keys by 429 count (stacked) + sparkline of burst usage per key. Add alert link and one-click runbook.
nate: Playbook stub for CS (short):
- Triage: confirm 429s are from one key, capture sample requests and timestamps.
- Mitigate: temporary soft-throttle (block high qps for 1m buckets) or set per-key burst_limit=0.5 via internal admin API.
- Engage: open CS ticket, attach traces, ask customer to reduce client concurrency or implement jitter/backoff.
- Follow-up: propose longer-term quota bump or dedicated throughput if justified.
mike: Command to set soft-throttle (internal admin):
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/keys/k_9f2a/throttle" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"burst_limit":0.5,"duration_s":300}'
```
alisha: Who's taking contact with the customer? need their account id. ops-bot, can you attach recent billing/org id?
ops-bot: org_id=org_4421, account_owner=eng-customer-ops@acme.co, billing_tier=standard. Added CS ticket CS-4871.
sam: I'll take initial outreach. @mike please run the admin curl to apply a 5m soft-throttle now if you agree.
mike: Applying now. Will monitor 1/5/15m windows and revert if we see customer impact beyond expected.
eva: Post-mortem notes: add a perf regression check in rollout pipeline for token refill logic; consider a guardrail that prevents setting refill_rate below 0.05 for public keys.
alisha: +1 on guardrail. Also add a telemetry tag on alerts: 'per_key_focus' so CS+SRE get the right routing.
sam: Action items: Mike -> execute throttle (in progress). Alisha -> add Prom rule + retry metric (today). Eva -> dashboard panel update (EOD). Sam -> customer outreach (now). Nate -> write short CS playbook doc and link in alert (tomorrow).
mike: Confirmed throttle applied at 1779001245. Monitoring.
sam: Thanks all. If 429s persist after throttle we escalate to account team and discuss dedicated capacity.
ops-bot: UPDATE: 429 rate reduced from 7.2% -> 1.1% within 3m after throttle. Closing automated escalation, CS ticket remains open. :white_check_mark:
